Hannah / Monica,

Thanks for taking this — attached is our short security questionnaire focused on where data lives (regions), retention windows, and deletion/erasure proof for hosted endpoints. We have a few requirements we need to validate before we can complete procurement:

- Can you confirm which AWS regions you support for the hosted API and whether we can pin a tenant to a single region?
- Retention windows for request logs, generated content (model outputs), embeddings, and backups — please provide default retention and any enterprise options.
- Do backups or snapshots ever cross regions? If so, under what conditions?
- What is the operational process and SLA for a customer-initiated erasure (delete all historic content for a tenant)? Any attestations you can provide are helpful.

We appreciate concise, itemized answers we can include in our security review. If you can attach any short diagrams or a retention matrix, that would be ideal.

Hi Daniel / Gina —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are itemized answers for the hosted API (we also attach a short residency diagram + a retention matrix). I kept responses practical and linked to the configuration options available to customers on Redwood’s hosted offering. If you want a one-page summary for procurement I can export one.

1) Regions / region pinning
- Supported regions: us-west-2 (Oregon), us-east-1 (N. Virginia), eu-west-1 (Ireland). We are adding ap-southeast-1 (Singapore) later in 2028; ETA Q3.
- Tenant pinning: hosted tenants can be pinned to a primary region at account creation. For regulated customers we recommend pinning; the control plane remains global but customer data and persistent stores are constrained to the pinned region by configuration.

2) Retention: defaults and enterprise options (hosted API)
- Request logs (full request/response metadata, excluding ephemeral cache): default 30 days; enterprise retention options: 90 days / 365 days via add-on.
- Generated content (model outputs and any persisted completions): default 30 days. Customers may request custom TTLs or choose not to persist completions by enabling “no-persist” mode in account settings (forcible no-persist is available under enterprise plans).
- Embeddings: default 365 days; may be set to 30/90/365 or to manual retention by customer on enterprise tiers.
- Metrics & aggregated telemetry: retained for 13 months for product analytics and SLA trending (aggregated, not PII).
- Audit logs (control-plane events): retained 1 year by default; exportable on demand to customer S3 for longer retention.

3) Backups and snapshots
- Backups: periodic snapshots of the persistent layer (encrypted) are retained for 90 days by default.
- Cross-region replication: backups do not cross regions by default. Cross-region replication is only enabled when explicitly configured for disaster recovery or by enterprise contract. If enabled, replication is restricted to a pre-approved DR region and is documented in the contract.

4) Deletion / erasure process & SLA
- Soft-delete + purge model: customer-initiated erasure sets a soft-delete marker and triggers the following automated pipeline:
  a) Remove pointers from live indexes and mark data tombstoned (near-real time).
  b) Remove cached keys/kv from in-memory caches within minutes.
  c) Enqueue records for physical purge from persistent stores and object stores.
- SLA: standard hosted pipeline completes full physical purge within 30 days of request (this covers eventual consistency, backups, and queued snapshots). For enterprise customers with a documented erasure SLA, we can compress this to 7–14 days and provide an attestation once completed.
- Evidence: after purge we can provide a deletion certificate (signed) that enumerates the artifacts removed and timestamps. For regulated customers we offer a one-time independent verification (third-party attestation) as a billable add-on.

5) Encryption & key management (hosted)
- Data at rest and in transit: all customer data in hosted API is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256).
- Keys: hosted accounts use Redwood-managed keys by default. Customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) are available for enterprise customers via our Dedicated/Private options or as a hosted add-on when contractually required.

6) Logs and access for support/ops
- Support staff access to tenant data is tightly controlled and audited. Access is granted via just-in-time roles with approver workflows for any access to customer plaintext content. All access is logged and retained per audit log retention above.

7) Evidence & artifacts we can provide immediately
- Residency diagram (attached): shows region scoping for live data vs control plane.
- Retention matrix (attached) showing default vs enterprise options.
- Deletion certificate template and sample (we can issue post-purge).
- SOC 2 Type II summary (we can share redacted report under NDA).

Notes / caveats:
- For the hosted API, short-lived caches (prefix/KV caches used by inference runtime) are best-effort ephemeral and are not considered long-term storage; cache eviction is workload-dependent. If strict non-persistence is required, we recommend our enterprise setting to disable storage of completions and use a dedicated rollout.
- Where cross-region replication is required for DR, please include the DR region in your procurement paperwork so we can ensure contract and technical alignment.

I’ve attached the two files (residency-2028.pdf and retention_matrix_2028.csv). Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you’d rather walk through this.

Thanks,

Daniel / Hannah — quick operational clarifications from an infra perspective to add to Hannah's note:

- Snapshot lifecycle detail: persistent snapshots are stored in the same region as the primary store unless DR replication is configured. Snapshot objects are subject to lifecycle policies that permanently delete snapshot objects 90 days after creation unless retained for a specific ticketed retention extension.
- Object storage purge: after the soft-delete window we run a two-pass purge (mark -> queue -> garbage collect) to prevent accidental data loss. This does mean small windows where data exists in pending deletion state — these windows are covered by our 30-day purge SLA.
- Backups and ephemeral caches: ephemeral GPU-level cache (model KV caches) live on instance local NVMe and are ephemeral by design; they are never written to snapshots or S3. Only persistent user artifacts are included in backups.
- Emergency/expedited erasure: for legal holds or emergency erasures we have an expedited workflow; we will require a signed PO or contract amendment for guaranteed 7-day expedited purge to ensure capacity and scheduling.

If you need exact retention timestamps for a subset of tenants, we can export a CSV with creation and deletion timestamps after we complete the purge.

—Monica
Principal Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
